record.original_question: For the Aztec window obtained by deleting a centered Aztec diamond of order x from an outer Aztec diamond of order y, find a general formula for the number of domino tilings. In particular, explain the observed polynomial dependence on x when y=x+w for fixed even w.

evidence.quote: Let us define the Aztec window with outer order y and inner order x to be the Aztec diamond of order y with an Aztec diamond of order x deleted from its center.
Problem 14: Find a general formula for the number of domino tilings of Aztec windows.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Aztec diamond of order n is the union of all unit lattice squares [i,i+1]×[j,j+1] (i,j ∈ ℤ) whose centers (i+1/2, j+1/2) satisfy |i+1/2| + |j+1/2| ≤ n. A domino is a 1×2 or 2×1 rectangle consisting of two unit squares sharing an edge, and a domino tiling of a region is a covering of the region by non-overlapping dominoes.

For positive integers x < y, define the Aztec window W(y, x) to be the region obtained from the Aztec diamond of order y by deleting a centrally placed Aztec diamond of order x (with the same center of symmetry).

(a) Determine a general closed-form expression for the number T(y, x) of domino tilings of W(y, x).

(b) Fix an even positive integer w and set y = x + w. Establish and explain the observation that T(x+w, x), as a function of x, is given by a polynomial in x (whose degree and leading behaviour may depend on w), and identify this polynomial.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2025) on "Round Aztec windows" notes that the original tiling counts for Aztec windows (with an Aztec-diamond shaped hole) are not given by a simple product formula. That work instead considers modified hole shapes (odd Aztec rectangles) which do admit product formulas, thereby sidestepping rather than resolving the original problem. No closed-form general formula for T(y,x) appears to be known.

status_evidence.title: Round Aztec windows, a dual of the Aztec diamond theorem...
status_evidence.snippet: the numbers themselves are not 'round' — they didn't seem to be given by a simple product formula; changing the window to an odd Aztec diamond yields product formulas
status_evidence.claim: The original Aztec window tiling-count problem lacks a simple product formula and is addressed only via a modified version of the problem.
